_instructions: Watch data/raw/freeflowbasketball_oxnard.mp4 (or use the frontend video player) at each start_ts-end_ts window. Fill in ball_handler_track_id with the GLOBAL player ID (see game_state.json roster.track_id_to_name / unmapped_track_ids) who had the ball for most of the possession, and outcome with one of: made_2, made_3, missed, turnover, foul, unknown. The _pipeline_predicted_* fields are the perception pipeline's own guess, shown only as a reference hint -- do not treat them as correct, that is exactly what this file is checking. Known issue: player identity (track IDs) is unreliable across possessions (documented in game_state.json meta.notes), so the SAME real player may show a different _pipeline_predicted_handler ID in different possessions -- judge each possession by what you actually see in the video, not by ID consistency.

_labeling_method: possessions p001-p015 were human-verified: the project owner watched each clip in data/processed/clips/ directly and confirmed or corrected the outcome. This caught two real errors in the initial Claude-drafted labels -- p007 (labeled made_2, actually stops after a normal pass with no shot) and p013 (labeled made_2, actually a missed shot) -- showing the 'cut always follows a make' assumption doesn't hold for every possession. possessions p016-p027 remain Claude-drafted from that same editing-convention assumption and have NOT been independently reviewed; treat that portion as a weaker, directional signal only. ball_handler_track_id was left unlabeled throughout -- verifying it independently requires either ID-overlay video or manual position-matching against game_state.json, neither of which was feasible in the time available.
